function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

message.content:
Pizza’s roots trace back to ancient flatbreads topped with herbs and olive oil—think early Mediterranean cultures like the Greeks (pita) and Romans (panis focacius). However, the modern concept of “pizza” as we know it began in **Naples, Italy**, around the late 18th‑early 19th centuries. Neapolitan cooks added tomato sauce (introduced to Europe only after the Columbian Exchange), mozzarella cheese, basil, and other simple toppings, creating what many consider the classic Margherita style.

From there, Italian immigrants carried their recipes across the globe—in the United States, South America, Australia, and beyond—leading to countless regional adaptations while keeping the core idea of a dough base topped with flavorful ingredients. So, while similar dishes existed elsewhere historically, **the contemporary pizza originated in Naples, Italy**.
